message.content:
The exact count of mitochondria per cell isn’t fixed—it varies widely with cell type, developmental stage, and metabolic demand. In most mammalian somatic cells you’ll find roughly **50–200 mitochondria** per cell, though this can rise dramatically in high‑energy tissues:

| Cell type | Approximate mitochondria per cell |
|-----------|-----------------------------------|
| Neurons (especially axons) | 100–1 000+ |
| Skeletal muscle fibers | 500–5 000+ |
| Cardiac myocytes | 1 000–10 000+ |
| Hepatocytes | 200–1 000+ |
| Erythrocytes (mature) | 0 (they lose mitochondria during maturation) |

These numbers are averages; individual cells can differ by orders of magnitude. Counting methods include electron microscopy (direct visualization), flow cytometry with mitochondrial dyes, or biochemical assays measuring mitochondrial DNA copy number.
